hook_text: Your house has a street address. So does every spot on Earth, written in just two numbers.
clip_script: Imagine wrapping the whole Earth in a giant net. Some strings go round it like belts: those are lines of latitude, counting north or south from the equator. Other strings go from the top to the bottom, like the lines on a peeled orange: those are lines of longitude, counting east or west from a line through Greenwich in London. Every place on the planet sits where two strings cross. Cape Town? Thirty-four degrees south, eighteen degrees east. Two numbers, and a pilot, a ship's captain or a rescue team anywhere in the world knows exactly where to go. And here is the trick that loses marks: latitude always comes first, and the letters N, S, E or W are not optional. Thirty-four south is near Cape Town. Thirty-four north is near Morocco.
visual_style: A whiteboard globe being wrapped in a net of lines; a pin drops on Cape Town; the numbers 34 S and 18 E write themselves beside it, then a second pin flips to the Northern Hemisphere.
pacing: Fast hook, a slow reveal of the grid, a punchy ending on the common mistake.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and give any place on Earth its address.
